reason: Both correctly identify these as normal refrigerant, thermostat and expansion noises with no part or engineer needed, matching the hidden truth. Conversation 1 gives the right escalation trigger (squealing, grinding, loud rattling) which is exactly the abnormal-noise boundary the homeowner should watch for. Conversation 2 explains the mechanisms in more helpful detail and sensibly ties normalcy to food staying cold, but its fault criteria are weaker: 'warm to the touch' is misleading (cabinet sides normally run warm from the condenser) and 'oily residue' hints at a refrigerant leak, which is unsupported and mildly alarmist, while it omits the loud buzzing/grinding trigger. Neither asked about level, clearance or displayed temperatures, so the edge to 1 is only slight.
